case_analysis.focal_point: Whether the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits a state from requiring a corporation to consent to general personal jurisdiction as a condition of doing business within its borders (i.e., 'registration jurisdiction').
case_analysis.legal_provision: Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment
case_analysis.petitioner_position: The petitioner argues that the Due Process Clause does not prohibit a state from requiring a corporation to consent to general personal jurisdiction as a condition of doing business in the state. Therefore, 'registration jurisdiction' is constitutionally permissible.
case_analysis.respondent_position: The respondent argues that the Due Process Clause does prohibit a state from requiring a corporation to consent to general personal jurisdiction as a condition of doing business, thus rendering 'registration jurisdiction' unconstitutional.
key_precedents: Insurance Corp. of Ireland v. Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée
